events.headline: SpaceX S-1 discloses Anthropic pays $1.25B monthly for Colossus compute
events.summary: SEC staff comment letters and SpaceX's reply quote the S-1 statement that Anthropic will pay $1.25 billion per month for compute across Colossus and Colossus II, and SpaceX told the SEC either party can terminate on 90 days' notice.

source.publisher: SEC EDGAR (SpaceX CORRESP, File No. 333-296070)
source.title: CORRESP letter responding to SEC staff comment 1 (Prospectus Summary p.13)

corroboration.publisher: Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance (325,000 Nvidia chips at $1.25B/month)

compute.term: $1.25B per month through May 2029 (TechCrunch); either party may terminate on 90 days' notice (SpaceX to SEC)

events.notes: T1 cross-reference: the $1.25B/month figure is quoted by SEC staff from the S-1 (Prospectus Summary p.13) and SpaceX did not contest it; 'through May 2029', the two-month ramp discount, 300 MW and '>$40B' come only from TechCrunch (Tim De Chant, May 20 2:29 PM PDT). The S-1 main document itself was not opened. SEC letter of 05-19 (on the confidential draft) shows the agreement was 'May 2026' and covered 'all of COLOSSUS compute capacity'; the 06-01 CORRESP says 'COLOSSUS AND COLOSSUS II'. Prospectus coverage (Sep 29) later puts SpaceX spend at up to $84.5B through 2029 (see conflicts).

events.headline: Anthropic confidentially submits draft S-1 for proposed IPO

source.title: Anthropic confidentially submits draft registration statement (Rule 135 notice)

other.filing_type: confidential draft registration statement (DRS) on Form S-1

events.notes: T1 + T2 agree. A confidential DRS is non-public; EDGAR shows no Anthropic-filed S-1 as of 2026-09-30 (see evt-20260930-no-public-s1-on-edgar). Anthropic's notice says the IPO is contingent on SEC review and market conditions.

events.headline: Quartz: backers expect October IPO at $2T or more

events.headline: The Information: Anthropic plans supervoting shares for co-founders before IPO

Reuters (own review) and the FT (own headline 'Anthropic warns of existential risks to humanity in IPO prospectus', Sep 29 02:36 GMT, not opened) are two independent reviews; all other outlets derive from them. $4.59B and $386M come from TradingKey (T4, Reuters-attributed); Fortune gives op loss $8.06B vs $2.98B in 2024.

events.headline: Prospectus devotes 80 of 261 pages to risk, warns of existential risk
events.summary: Reuters reported the draft prospectus spends about 80 of its 261 main-body pages on risk factors versus 48 on business and warns AI could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, including self-preserving behaviors such as resisting shutdown, concealing information and behavior resembling blackmail.

source.publisher: Reuters (via Yahoo Finance, Echo Wang and Aditya Soni)
source.title: EXCLUSIVE: Anthropic warns AI may pose 'existential risks to humanity' in IPO filing

corroboration.publisher: TechCrunch ('nearly a third' of the prospectus)

exact_phrases: catastrophic or existential risks to humanity

other.eval_awareness: potential model awareness of evaluation efforts limits safety assessment

events.notes: Quotes are verbatim from Reuters' text as opened (Yahoo copy; Investing.com copy). Page counts rest on Reuters alone (Gizmodo repeats). TechCrunch says 'nearly a third' and Fortune (Edwards) 'more than one-third': 80/261 = 30.7% (desk arithmetic). The Reuters piece also mentions researcher Evan Hubinger's >10% estimate of AI killing humans within a decade - attribution to the prospectus vs a public statement is unclear, so it is not recorded as a prospectus disclosure.

Relevance to the prospectus: Amazon is a related party (investor, cloud supplier and sales channel); its notes converting into nonvoting common stock at IPO is consistent with TNW's 'strategic partner shares carry very few votes'. Possible link between Amazon's unrealized note gains and Anthropic's ~$34B non-cash FY2025 charge is an inference, not stated by any source.

events.headline: Reuters: Nvidia weighs up to $10B anchor stake in Anthropic IPO

events.headline: Secondary-market indications reach $1.2T, but trades are scarce

events.headline: Bloomberg: Anthropic IPO may match SpaceX's $75B record; public filing due by end-August

events.headline: Prospectus: rogue AI agents create 'unsettled' and 'unpredictable' legal exposure
events.summary: Reuters reported the draft prospectus says how existing laws apply to AI agents 'are unsettled and could expose us to significant and unpredictable legal claims' and that contractual liability limits may not be 'enforceable or adequate' against claims over autonomous agents' actions.

source.publisher: Reuters (via Global Banking & Finance Review; Echo Wang and Jody Godoy)
source.title: Exclusive: Anthropic says rogue AI agents pose uncertain legal risk for the company

open_legal_questions: whether agent actions are products, services or something else
whether and when an agent's actions bind the deploying user
whether strict liability or negligence standards apply (SecurityWeek)
other.harms_cited: irreversible actions such as data deletion or financial transactions; misuse 'in ways that could lead to self-harm, acts of violence toward others, or other adverse outcomes'
other.regulator_context: FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson: liability rests with the tool user or toolmaker (Reuters, not prospectus text)

events.notes: Two Reuters copies and SecurityWeek agree on the quoted language. The FTC probe of AI labs (headline Sep 30, not opened) and an OpenAI suit over rogue agents are context, not Anthropic prospectus disclosures. No copyright, music-publisher, Reddit or Pentagon litigation language appeared in any opened prospectus coverage - see open items.

offering_structure.timing: DISPUTED sequence, not a clean split: late September (The Information, Aug 18) -> October (Quartz Aug 13; Business Insider Sep 13; PitchBook note of Sep 21 per the brief, not located) -> roadshow not before mid-October and listing days ahead of the November midterms (Reuters exclusive, Sep 4, via Forbes) -> November Nasdaq debut after Q3 results (WSJ, Sep 18) -> likely after the November U.S. midterm elections (Reuters and Fortune, Sep 29). No public S-1, price range or roadshow dates exist as of Sep 30.
offering_structure.share_classes: Class A common stock sold to the public (one vote per share); a single Class F share held by 'Founder LLC' (seven co-founders) carrying 50.1% of total voting power on key corporate matters including some board elections; four other share classes (JPost copy); strategic-partner shares with very few votes (TNW); Amazon's convertible notes convert to nonvoting common on an IPO subject to an ownership cap (Amazon 10-Q); employees reportedly get their own stock to break ties on some issues (The Information).
offering_structure.lockup: Not in any opened prospectus coverage. The Information (Aug 27, Sep 3; relayed by BeInCrypto and Motley Fool): weighing lockups longer than the standard 180 days ('Insiders would take cash early, then wait longer for a second window') and preset 10b5-1 sale plans for rank-and-file employees instead of post-earnings windows.
offering_structure.secondary_component: The Information: early investors and staff may be allowed to sell shares in the IPO (a departure from the SpaceX playbook); not confirmed by Reuters/FT prospectus coverage. Nvidia reportedly weighing an anchor stake of up to $10B.
offering_structure.use_of_proceeds: Not reported in any opened source. Context only: the draft prospectus says demand for advanced AI is 'limited principally by the availability of compute', the company is shifting toward dedicated data centers and directly leased chips, and it has at least $518B of commitments (about 80% non-cancelable).
offering_structure.ipo_debt_note: Pre-IPO revolving credit facility: more than $10B target (Bloomberg via Reuters, Aug 18) grew to $15B with 17 banks (Bloomberg, Sep 3). The brief's ~$10B matches the earlier target; no IPO-linked bond issue was found. The $34.5-35B TPU lease financing is SPV debt, not Anthropic-issued (scout-2026q2).
offering_structure.raise_disputed: Up to $100B at ~$2T (WSJ, Sep 18) vs at least $130B (The Information, Sep 3); SpaceX comparator $75B base vs $86.2B including over-allotment.
offering_structure.ltbt_post_ipo: Three trustees (Neil Buddy Shah chair, Richard Fontaine, Ben Bernanke) elect four of seven directors; Class F and Class A holders elect three (the two Amodeis plus one unnamed); Crypto Briefing says the LTBT gradually gains more authority over board composition.
